A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIPGuard/VIPBench study, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 ends after the references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes Appendices A–E. Newly supplied appendix material can be compared as added documentation, without assuming its experiments were newly conducted.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments on VIPEval, CelebDF and DF40, comparisons with other MLLMs, and model-generated explanations in Tables 1–4 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports annotation-free customization, component ablations, adaptive token selection, corruption tests and further explanation examples.

M1.justification: The three-stage VIPGuard architecture remains intact. Appendix D.3 adds Adaptive VIPGuard, which uses face recognition to select the appropriate VIP token automatically. Section 5.1 also introduces a Stage 3 variant without textual annotations. These are limited procedural extensions; expanded attention formulas and implementation disclosures do not establish a redesigned core method.

E1.justification: The underlying training sources, 22-identity VIPEval benchmark, forgery generators, CelebDF and DF40 coverage remain unchanged. v2 adds evaluation under Gaussian noise, blur and JPEG compression, plus automatic identity/token selection when multiple VIPs are protected. These extend input and deployment scenarios within the existing task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same conventional detectors, identity-aware methods and MLLM competitors. The added backbone, face-recognition component and training-stage comparisons vary VIPGuard itself rather than add competing detectors to those benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial controlled variation: textual supervision in Stage 3, training-stage combinations, available authentic-image counts, token lengths from 8 to 128, and 3B/7B/11B backbones. Appendix D.4 specifies three intensities for each corruption. These are additional experimental protocols; newly disclosed settings for the retained experiments are reproducibility information rather than evidence of rerunning them.

E4.justification: v1 mentions supplementary ablations but supplies none. v2 provides stage-removal, reference-image-count, token-size, backbone and face-recognition-component analyses, along with annotation-free and adaptive-selection comparisons and corruption robustness tests. Figures 8–11 also add genuine-pair and forgery explanation cases beyond the retained Figure 5 examples.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, detector-training seed studies, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added results remain point estimates. Varying generation seeds to create synthetic images was already described in v1 and is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. v2 adds extensive results in Tables 5–10 and Figures 6–11, including adaptive selection averaging 98.01% AUC versus 98.23% with supplied tokens, and strongest-noise performance of 94.12%. Table 5 reports image-only customization at 95.86%, but its annotated InSwap value of 99.43% conflicts with 96.40% in Table 1, limiting interpretation of that comparison.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly formalizes the exclusion of source identities from the available reference set. The written autoregressive losses change conditioning from the preceding token to the full preceding sequence, and attention inputs are explicitly defined. No theorem or proof is added. Equation 7 nevertheless includes fquery although adjacent prose says that representation is replaced by the VIP token.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: personalized detection as fine-grained identity recognition, the three-stage multimodal VIPGuard framework, VIPBench, and superior detection and explainability. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability boundaries: sensitivity to head rotations exceeding roughly 50 degrees, age differences, and limited use of audio or temporal information. It also adds interpretations concerning stage synergy, possible token overfitting, transfer enabling annotation-free customization, and semantic cues explaining corruption robustness. These qualifications and mechanisms were not developed in the supplied v1.

D1.justification: Appendices D.1 and E supply previously unavailable optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, epoch, resizing and prediction-scoring details, plus face filtering, sampling ratios and annotation prompts. TransFace is identified as the default similarity model. The release-on-acceptance promise is supplemented by a code URL and noncommercial, reviewed-request dataset access terms; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including FakeShield, AvatarShield and VLforgery Face Triad, expands the discussion of the already cited X2-DFD, and explicitly contrasts its unseen-source setting with prior identity-aware assumptions in Section 4.1. The broader positioning around personalized semantic detection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original main-text prose, contribution bullets and the conclusion are retained. Changes include localized copyediting, separating problem formulation from method overview, revising reference/query terminology, adding an annotation-free subsection and appendix roadmap, and updating publication and funding text. The supplementary expansion primarily adds content rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with ablation curves, robustness and variant tables, full explanation conversations, facial-attribute examples, annotation prompts and dataset-construction diagrams. Tables 1–4 are relocated or reformatted while retaining their results; existing diagrams and captions receive smaller revisions. The new displays make previously unavailable analyses and procedures inspectable.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important gaps in the supplied v1, which referred readers to unavailable supplementary support. Stage/component ablations, corruption tests, detailed training and data-construction procedures, and concrete failure conditions substantially strengthen evidential support and reproducibility despite unchanged headline scores. The conflicting InSwap value in Table 5 and inconsistent feature notation in Equation 7 are drawbacks, while uncertainty reporting remains absent. These limitations temper but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in assessability and transparency.
